goldens.comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:131 — Supplying any nonempty totpCode alongside a valid backupCode skips the password check at line 121, allowing the backup code to authenticate as the sole factor.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in next-auth-options.ts, the password check happens at lines 118-125 (checking isCorrectPassword) BEFORE the 2FA checks. The condition at line 128 is 'if (user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode)' which only handles backup code verification AFTER password has already been validated. The finding claims that supplying a totpCode alongside backupCode skips password check, but the password verification occurs unconditionally before any 2FA logic. The flow is: 1) verify password (lines 118-125), 2) if 2FA enabled AND backupCode provided, verify backup code (lines 128-152), 3) else if 2FA enabled, verify TOTP (lines 153+). There's no way to skip the password check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:135 — Backup codes are revealed only after the enable response arrives, so a committed enable followed by a lost response leaves 2FA active while its recovery codes remain permanently undisplayed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx, the flow is: (1) handleSetup generates backup codes and stores them server-side at line 89-97, (2) user scans QR code, (3) handleEnable verifies TOTP and on success sets step to DisplayBackupCodes at line 132. If the enable API call succeeds (2FA is now active server-side) but the response is lost due to network issues before line 132 executes, the user never sees the backup codes. The codes were already generated and stored during setup, so they exist but were never displayed. This is a real race condition/reliability bug where 2FA gets enabled but recovery codes are lost.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:278 — The clipboard write is neither awaited nor caught before the success toast, so permission or focus failures falsely tell users that their recovery codes were saved.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at line 278 in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx, the code calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText(backupCodes.map(formatBackupCode).join("\n"))` followed immediately by `showToast(t("backup_codes_copied"), "success")`. The clipboard API returns a Promise, but the code neither awaits it nor handles potential errors. If the clipboard write fails (due to permissions, focus issues, or browser restrictions), the success toast will still be shown, misleading users into thinking their backup codes were copied when they weren't. This is a real bug in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:131 — A caller can submit a valid backupCode plus any nonempty totpCode to skip password verification, turning the backup code into a single-factor login.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that submitting a valid backupCode plus any nonempty totpCode would skip password verification. Looking at the diff in next-auth-options.ts, the password verification happens BEFORE the 2FA check (lines 118-126 check password with verifyPassword). The 2FA logic (backup code or TOTP) only runs after password is already verified. The conditional at line 128 checks 'if (user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode)' which handles backup code authentication, and the 'else if (user.twoFactorEnabled)' handles TOTP. Password verification is not bypassed in either case - it's a prerequisite that happens earlier in the flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:61 — The new backupCode body field is used as a string without validation, so truthy non-string JSON produces an unhandled 500 instead of a client error.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in disable.ts lines 46-63, the code checks `if (user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode)` and then uses `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll('-', '')`. If backupCode is a truthy non-string value (like an object or array from JSON), calling replaceAll() on it would throw a TypeError, resulting in an unhandled 500 error. The code doesn't validate that backupCode is actually a string before calling string methods on it. This is a real input validation bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:131 — Supplying a valid backupCode together with any nonempty totpCode skips the earlier password check yet enters this branch, allowing authentication with the backup code alone.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, the password check happens at lines 118-126 in next-auth-options.ts (before the 2FA checks). The password verification using `verifyPassword(credentials.password, user.password)` occurs unconditionally before any 2FA logic. The backup code branch at line 131 only executes after the password has already been verified. The finding incorrectly claims that supplying a backup code skips the password check, but the code structure shows password verification happens first, then 2FA verification (either via backup code or TOTP) happens afterward.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:149 — Backup-code consumption performs an unconditional read-modify-write, so concurrent requests can both authenticate with the same one-time code or restore another request's consumed code.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows at lines 128-160 in next-auth-options.ts that backup code verification reads the backupCodes array, checks if the code exists (indexOf), then sets that index to null and writes back. This is a classic read-modify-write race condition - two concurrent requests with the same backup code could both read the array before either writes, both find the code valid, and both authenticate. The update is not atomic and there's no locking mechanism shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:278 — The clipboard write promise is ignored and a success toast is always shown, so denied or failed copies can leave users believing they saved recovery codes when they did not.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff at lines 270-278 in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx, the click handler calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText(backupCodes.map(formatBackupCode).join("\n"))` which returns a Promise, but this Promise is not awaited or handled with .then()/.catch(). The `showToast(t("backup_codes_copied"), "success")` is called immediately after, regardless of whether the clipboard operation succeeded or failed. This means if clipboard access is denied or fails, users will still see a success toast, potentially believing they saved their backup codes when they did not. This is a real bug affecting user experience and potentially security (users may lose access to their account if they think they copied codes but didn't).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/prisma/migrations/20230804153419_add_backup_codes/migration.sql:2 — Existing 2FA users remain NULL and setup rejects enabled accounts, so they cannot obtain backup codes without disabling and re-enabling 2FA.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the migration adds a nullable backupCodes column, meaning existing users with 2FA enabled will have NULL backupCodes. Looking at the setup.ts code, backup codes are only generated during the 2FA setup flow (when twoFactorEnabled is false initially). The code in next-auth-options.ts throws ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes if user.backupCodes is null when trying to use backup code login. This means existing 2FA users cannot use backup codes without disabling and re-enabling 2FA. This is a legitimate migration/upgrade path concern, though it's more of a product decision/edge case than a bug - the feature works correctly for new 2FA setups.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx:49 — Hard-coding tabIndex=-1 in the shared PasswordField removes the visibility control from keyboard navigation in every password form, coupling this feature's focus change to unrelated screens.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows tabIndex={-1} being added to the password visibility toggle button in the shared PasswordField component. This is a real change that removes the button from keyboard tab navigation. While this may be intentional for the 2FA flow (to prevent focus issues), it does affect all uses of PasswordField across the application. This is a legitimate architectural/scope concern - a change made for one feature affecting a shared component. However, it's not clearly a bug since removing decorative toggle buttons from tab order is sometimes an accessibility best practice (the password can still be typed without the toggle).

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts:61 — The 10-character backup-code format is duplicated here, in the formatter, and in input length limits, so changing generation can silently truncate or reject otherwise valid codes.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the backup code format (10 characters) is defined in multiple places: generation in setup.ts (crypto.randomBytes(5).toString('hex') = 10 chars), the formatBackupCode function that splits at position 5, and the BackupCode.tsx input with minLength=10/maxLength=11. While this is a valid maintainability concern about magic numbers being duplicated, it's not a bug since all the values are currently consistent. The concern about 'silently truncate or reject' is speculative - the current implementation works correctly. This is a legitimate code quality observation about coupling/duplication but not a defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:148 — Replacing a consumed code with null makes the stored array nullable while every handler treats the decrypted JSON as an untyped string array.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows at line 148 that when a backup code is consumed, it's replaced with `null` in the array (`backupCodes[index] = null`). However, looking at the code that validates backup codes (both in next-auth-options.ts line 140 and disable.ts line 64), they use `backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))` to check if the code exists. When `indexOf` is called on an array containing `null` values, it will still work for finding string codes, but the array now contains mixed types (strings and nulls). This could cause issues if code elsewhere expects a pure string array, though the immediate indexOf check would still function. The finding is partially valid - the array does become mixed-type, but the immediate functionality appears preserved since indexOf(-1) check still works for valid codes and null !== any valid backup code string.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:71 — resetState leaves backup codes, the blob URL, the TOTP secret, and form state intact, so closing the flow retains stale sensitive state and an unreleased object URL.

apps/web/components/settings/DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:38 — twoFactorLostAccess is cleared only after a successful disable, so cancelling and reopening a mounted modal resumes in stale backup-code mode.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, twoFactorLostAccess state is initialized at line 38 and only reset to false inside handleDisable when response.status === 200 (lines 57-58). The onCancel callback is passed as a prop and called directly without resetting twoFactorLostAccess. If a user clicks 'Lost access' to switch to backup code mode, then cancels the modal, and the modal component remains mounted (which is common in React dialogs), reopening it would show the backup code input instead of the TOTP input. The resetForm function exists but doesn't reset twoFactorLostAccess, and onCancel doesn't call resetForm or setTwoFactorLostAccess(false).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:149 — Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write, so concurrent requests can both authenticate with the same one-time code.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows backup code verification at lines 128-155 in next-auth-options.ts. The code reads backupCodes, checks if the user-supplied code exists in the array (indexOf), then sets that index to null and updates the database. This is a classic read-modify-write race condition: two concurrent requests could both read the same backupCodes array before either writes, both find the same code valid, and both authenticate successfully. The update is not atomic - there's no transaction or conditional update to ensure the code hasn't been used between read and write.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:135 — Deferring onEnable until the custom Close button means X/Escape dismissal after the server succeeds leaves the parent showing stale 2FA state.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that at line 132-135, when the TOTP code is successfully verified (response.status === 200), the code now calls setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes) instead of immediately calling onEnable(). The onEnable() is only called when the user clicks the 'Close' button (lines 263-270). However, the Dialog component has onOpenChange prop which handles X button and Escape key dismissal. If the user dismisses the dialog via X or Escape after the server successfully enables 2FA but before clicking the Close button, onEnable() is never called, leaving the parent component with stale state showing 2FA as disabled when it's actually enabled on the server.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:135 — A lost response after the enable endpoint commits strands the modal on the OTP step, while a retry cannot reach the only backup-code display path.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, when handleEnable succeeds (response.status === 200), it calls setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes) at line 135. However, the backup codes were already generated and stored during the setup phase (handleSetup), not during enable. If the network response is lost after the server commits the enable but before the client receives the 200, a retry of handleEnable would fail because 2FA is already enabled. The user would be stuck on the OTP step and never see the backup codes that were generated during setup. This is a real edge case bug where network issues could prevent users from ever seeing their backup codes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:278 — The clipboard promise is neither awaited nor caught, so denied or failed copies still show a success toast and produce an unhandled rejection.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at line 278 in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx, the code calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText(backupCodes.map(formatBackupCode).join("\n"))` without awaiting the promise or adding a .catch() handler. The `showToast(t("backup_codes_copied"), "success")` is called immediately after, regardless of whether the clipboard operation succeeded. This means: 1) If clipboard access is denied or fails, the success toast still shows (incorrect UX), and 2) The rejected promise is unhandled, causing an unhandled rejection error. This is a real bug in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:99 — The backup-code Blob URL is only revoked by a later setup, so closing or unmounting the modal retains its sensitive data and allocation until page unload.
matched_golden_ids: Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the same underlying problem as the golden comment - the Blob URL for backup codes is not being properly revoked when the component unmounts. The candidate mentions that the URL is 'only revoked by a later setup' and that 'closing or unmounting the modal retains its sensitive data and allocation until page unload', which is essentially describing the same memory leak issue caused by not revoking the Object URL on component unmount. The candidate also adds the security concern about sensitive data retention, but the core issue is the same.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:131 — Supplying any nonempty totpCode skips password verification and then lets this branch authenticate with only a valid backup code, reducing the intended two-factor flow to one factor.

adjudication.rationale: The finding misreads the code flow. Looking at the diff at line 128-165 in next-auth-options.ts, the password verification happens BEFORE the 2FA check (lines 126 and earlier verify password). The condition at line 128 is `if (user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode)` - this checks if backup code is provided. If a user provides a totpCode but not a backupCode, this branch is skipped and the else-if branch at line 157 handles TOTP verification. The backup code branch only executes when backupCode is explicitly provided. Password verification is not skipped - it happens before this 2FA logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:149 — Backup-code consumption uses an unconditional read-modify-write, so concurrent login requests can all validate and reuse the same supposedly one-time code.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows backup code validation at line 149 in next-auth-options.ts uses a read-modify-write pattern: it reads backupCodes, checks if the code exists with indexOf, then updates the database to remove it. Between the read and write, another concurrent request could validate the same backup code before it's marked as used. This is a classic TOCTOU (time-of-check-time-of-use) race condition that could allow a single backup code to be used multiple times for authentication, which is a security vulnerability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:12 — The new security feature has no test for backup-code login or backup-code 2FA disable, leaving acceptance, rejection, and one-time consumption behavior unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds significant new backup code functionality for 2FA (login with backup code, disabling 2FA with backup code, backup code generation and display). The test file at line 12 explicitly contains a TODO comment 'add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup' acknowledging this gap. While some backup code UI tests are added (download, copy, close buttons), there are no tests verifying the actual security-critical flows: logging in with a backup code, disabling 2FA with a backup code, or verifying one-time consumption of backup codes. This is a legitimate test coverage gap for newly added nontrivial security logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:50 — The added FIXME knowingly leaves `expect(locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` asserting a Promise, so a failed enable-state transition silently passes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows at line 50 a FIXME comment acknowledging that `expect(page.locator(`[data-testid=two-factor-switch]`).isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` is incorrect because `isChecked()` returns a Promise, not a boolean. This means the assertion will always pass (truthy Promise object) regardless of the actual checked state. The comment explicitly states 'this passes even when switch is not checked'. This is a real bug in the test code that was knowingly left in place, making the test unreliable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:116 — The download test asserts only the suggested filename, so an empty or malformed backup-code file still passes.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the test at line 116 only checks `download.suggestedFilename()` equals 'cal-backup-codes.txt' but doesn't verify the actual content of the downloaded file. The test even has a TODO comment '// TODO: check file content' acknowledging this gap. This is a legitimate test coverage concern for newly added backup code functionality - the download could be empty or malformed and the test would still pass. However, this is not a bug (the feature works), but rather incomplete test coverage for new functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:121 — The copy test waits only for an unconditional success toast, so clipboard write failures or incorrect copied codes still pass.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a new test at line 121 that clicks the copy button and waits for a success toast, but doesn't verify the actual clipboard content. The comment 'TODO: check clipboard content' at line 123 confirms this is an incomplete test. This is a valid concern about test coverage for newly added functionality - the test could pass even if the wrong content was copied. However, this is not a bug since the feature itself may work correctly; it's just that the test doesn't fully verify the behavior.
